Clients · projects · reports · segments · personas
Who is our highest-value segment in Texas?
Your core buyer is 35–44, urban female, HHI $80k+. They drive an outsized share of category spend and index high on convenience and trust signals.
How does that compare to the Florida project?
Florida's top segment shares the age band but skews suburban with stronger brand loyalty. Price sensitivity is lower — higher willingness to pay at shelf.
Pull all personas with high price sensitivity across active projects
Three personas match. Strongest signal in the Q1 CPG study — a 28–38 female, mid-income, convenience-driven buyer who price-compares on shelf. Want me to compare their purchase triggers?
Yes — and flag any overlap with the retail client's segments
Two overlap: the value-first buyer and the aspirational mid-income shopper appear in both. Retail client's version skews slightly older with stronger loyalty once converted. Same acquisition challenge, different retention profile.

Common Questions

What decision intelligence
actually means.

What is Fisga?

Fisga is a decision intelligence platform that helps CPG brands and operator teams answer go-to-market, pricing, and positioning decisions in minutes — grounded in U.S. federal data. Instead of waiting weeks for traditional research, Fisga delivers confident, defensible answers before capital is committed.

What is decision intelligence?

Decision intelligence is the practice of applying structured data analysis to answer specific business decisions before committing capital. Pricing, channel selection, market entry, brand positioning — each answered with directional confidence from real consumer and economic data, not instinct.

How is Fisga different from traditional market research?

Traditional market research takes 6–8 weeks and costs tens of thousands of dollars. Fisga delivers the same quality of insight in under 20 minutes — because the federal data infrastructure is already built. No panel recruitment. No fieldwork. Every finding traces to a named government dataset.

What kinds of decisions can Fisga answer?

Fisga is built for five decision types: feasibility (go/no-go), pricing (what the market will actually pay), positioning (which message lands), concept testing (pre-launch validation), and segmentation (who your real buyer is). Each delivers a specific, actionable answer.

What data does Fisga use?

Every Fisga study is grounded in U.S. federal datasets — including U.S. Census demographic data, Bureau of Labor Statistics consumer spending data, Federal Reserve economic indicators, and CDC behavioral health surveys. Every number has a source. Every insight is auditable.

How fast does Fisga deliver results?

Most Fisga studies complete in 10 to 20 minutes from brief submission — including executive summary, segment analysis, pricing architecture, and market scoring. The Einstieg go-to-market study: 16 minutes. The infrastructure is already built. The data is pre-loaded.
